newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Awaiting budget, NZ shines.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Awaiting budget, NZ shines.

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads were little changed against the U.S. and Canada as the local market marked-time ahead of the Federal budget later on Tuesday, but underperformed against a rebounding New Zealand debt market.

Long domestic bond yields struck their lowest level since late February at one stage during Tuesday's session in anticipation of a market-friendly budget, but thin liquidity curbed the rally, traders said.

Expectations of limited, or zero, net bond issuance for the next fiscal year due to projections of a substantial headline budget surplus for 1997/98 is expected to receive a positive response from the market, analysts said.

"In our view, the excellent prospects for Australian Government budgets for the remainder of the decade means that the spread between Australian 10-year bonds and offshore bonds of equivalent duration can narrow," said Dresdener Bank in its weekly review.
"We expect the spread to trend lower, back to the low 80 basis points (to the U.S.) and potentially lower over the coming few months," the report added.
Treasuer Peter Costello is due to hand down the 1997/98 budget at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).

Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries were mixed in Tokyo after giving up some ground on profit-taking in late New York having firmed in anticipation of weak retail sales data later on Tuesday and benign inflation reports later this week.

New Zealand bonds rebounded as a higher N.Z. TWI and further Eurokiwi bond issuance supported the market after Monday's sell-off on unexpected remarks by the RBNZ that it would prefer somewhat firmer monetary conditions.
